chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said:
I asked Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the permissibility of shooting birds at night while they are in their nests, so he said, 'There is no harm in that.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to hunt birds at night according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of hunting birds at night while they are resting in their nests (wakr), a ruling derived from the general principle of permissibility in hunting unless specific restrictions apply. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the distinction between the act of hunting itself and the conditions of the prey, affirming that the state of the bird (resting) does not invalidate the hunt. This ruling is often discussed alongside other hadiths that prohibit hunting animals while they are sleeping or grazing, emphasizing the ethical treatment of game.
